The main takeaway from our work is that
1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 and its metabolites are not all equally effective in stimulating the intestinal calcium-binding protein synthesis and the rise of the serum calcium level.
1,25(OH)2D3 is a more potent form of vitamin D compared to 1,25,24(OH)3D3 or 1,25-25(OH)3 D3.
